raw_response:
I would provisionally rebuild around Sonarr + Radarr + Bazarr, and evaluate MediaManager on a small separate sample before switching the main library. Your two stated priorities—subtitles for foreign-language programmes and seedbox integration—make the completeness of those workflows more important than the number of interfaces. This is a documentation-based recommendation; I have not deployed or tested either configuration.

## 1. Sonarr + Radarr + Bazarr — my first choice to evaluate

The strongest evidence I found for your subtitle needs is Bazarr's official setup guide. It documents connections to Sonarr and Radarr, selectable subtitle languages, language profiles, provider configuration, subtitle upgrades, and an automatic synchronization option. Those are directly relevant controls for managing subtitles across an existing TV/movie collection. They do not establish that a provider has good subtitles for your particular programmes and languages, so those should be tested with representative files. [Bazarr setup guide](https://wiki.bazarr.media/Getting-Started/Setup-Guide/)

For a seedbox, separate the download-client connection from access to the completed files. The indexed official Sonarr documentation describes monitoring downloads through the client's API, importing completed files, and translating reported remote paths into paths Sonarr can access. A path translation therefore does not by itself establish a working file-transfer or mounted-storage arrangement. The same documentation describes preserving torrent data for seeding and using hardlinks or copies when importing, subject to the filesystem and configuration. This evidence was available in an official-source search excerpt; direct wiki reads returned no readable text and a raw-source read was blocked. Treat the exact seedbox configuration as unresolved until a test import succeeds. [Official Sonarr settings source](https://github.com/Servarr/Wiki/blob/master/sonarr/settings.md)

My proposed setup is to keep the seedbox's downloader, connect the relevant media manager to it, make completed files accessible to that manager, and give Bazarr access to the resulting library. Choose the exact mounting or transfer method to fit the seedbox you already have. If the applications see different paths, configure the applicable mappings. This is a deployment outline, not confirmation that your unnamed provider, client, filesystem or permissions already satisfy it.

The useful acceptance test is one representative foreign-language episode: obtain it through the intended seedbox route, import it, confirm continued seeding where required by your workflow, fetch the desired subtitle language, and check playback and timing. Repeat with a movie if movies are in scope. A failure should identify whether the problem is downloader access, file visibility, matching, provider coverage or subtitle quality.

**Classification:** a combination of applications covering the proposed TV/movie management stack. **Assessment:** INSUFFICIENT for an unconditional end-to-end recommendation, because the seedbox environment and subtitle languages/providers are unspecified. It remains the better-supported first option to evaluate.

## 2. MediaManager — retain as an integrated alternative, with two specific checks

The official project describes a unified interface for discovering, managing and automating TV and movie collections. Its configuration documentation connects it to download clients and to Prowlarr or Jackett for indexer access. Plan around those documented components when judging how much administration the unified interface would save. [MediaManager](https://maxdorninger.github.io/MediaManager/latest/) · [Indexer configuration](https://maxdorninger.github.io/MediaManager/latest/configuration/indexers/)

The download-client documentation includes qBittorrent, Transmission and SABnzbd. It requires the download directories to be accessible to MediaManager; the Transmission section specifically requires matching paths to the same volume. Those statements support client integration, but they do not confirm every remote seedbox arrangement. Verify your exact client and how its completed files reach the server before assuming a complete replacement. [Download clients](https://maxdorninger.github.io/MediaManager/latest/configuration/download-clients/)

For subtitles, the import documentation explicitly includes existing subtitle files in the episode naming requirements. That is evidence about importing existing files. The sources I could inspect did not establish an automatic subtitle-provider workflow or a supported way to substitute MediaManager for Sonarr/Radarr in Bazarr's integration. I would leave those capabilities unknown rather than claim they are unsupported. [Importing existing media](https://maxdorninger.github.io/MediaManager/latest/importing-existing-media/)

The two decision-changing checks are therefore: can the intended MediaManager version obtain and manage the subtitle languages you need, and can it import successfully from your actual seedbox while preserving your desired seeding behaviour? Positive evidence on both would make it a credible whole-stack alternative. A documented incompatibility would narrow its usefulness; absence of documentation alone is insufficient grounds to exclude it.

When testing an existing-library import, use a sample copy: the import guide describes renaming the old root folders with a leading dot and requires season/episode identifiers in episode video and subtitle filenames. Check the resulting matches and paths before applying that workflow to the full collection. [Importing existing media](https://maxdorninger.github.io/MediaManager/latest/importing-existing-media/)

**Classification:** an application proposed as the main management replacement, with external integrations. **Assessment:** INSUFFICIENT for a verified replacement in this particular setup. It is retained, not rejected.

## Timing and missing context

The question is dated 8 January 2026. The accessible Bazarr guide displays a 19 November 2026 update, and the indexed Sonarr source displays an August 2026 revision. These establish later documented behaviour, not a complete historical feature comparison as of the question date. MediaManager's import page states 20 December 2025; its other live pages did not expose a reliable publication date. I have kept those distinctions explicit.

The supplied summary does not include the existing application list, linked prior discussions, exact subtitle languages, seedbox client, operating system or deployment versions. It also does not identify explicit mandatory exclusions. My ranking consequently favours the more directly documented subtitle workflow while leaving MediaManager eligible for the focused checks above.
